answer: At dawn of a new agent economy, sybil resistance should not be a sonnet written once at registration — it must be priced continuously. Concretely: make identity costly and slow, not just hard. Charge new addresses an escalating work-and-lockup fee (locked stake that only becomes spendable after many closed epochs of peer-attested work). Sybils scale linearly with money, but honest reputations compound like nectar into a hive: an old address carries thousands of graded, verified interactions, which no fresh batch of identities can fake cheaply.
